name: Real Estate
title: Commercial lease operations workbench
summary: Reconcile lease obligations, maintenance requests, and property records for manager-reviewed operational action.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A commercial property manager receives a tenant request involving an after-hours equipment repair and disputed service responsibility. Teams must locate lease amendments, asset records, and prior work orders before responding. The system supports document and facilities operations; qualified professionals resolve legal interpretation and contractual disputes.
problem: A base lease may be superseded by amendments, and property names may differ between finance and maintenance systems. Automatically declaring who must pay from a retrieved clause can misrepresent the agreement or expose another tenant's confidential terms.
whyAgents: Lease evidence, asset history, service coordination, and response specialists gather bounded facts. A property-scoped workflow separates document citations from legal interpretation and requires authorized approval for commitments or disputed obligations.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Measure preparation time and source accuracy while tracking unresolved disputes. The architecture should improve operational clarity without presenting its summaries as legal determinations or replacing established property-management authority.

agents.name: Lease evidence agent
agents.responsibility: Retrieve relevant clauses and amendments with execution dates and document references.
agents.boundary: Cannot provide legal advice or determine disputed contractual liability.

agents.name: Asset investigator
agents.responsibility: Locate equipment ownership, maintenance history, and open service requests.
agents.boundary: Cannot certify equipment safety or close unresolved defects.

agents.name: Service coordinator
agents.responsibility: Find approved vendors, availability, and property access requirements.
agents.boundary: Cannot award work or grant building access independently.

agents.name: Tenant response drafter
agents.responsibility: Compile factual status, cited documents, and proposed next steps.
agents.boundary: Cannot send binding notices or promise payment without review.

systems.name: Lease administration system
systems.role: Owns executed leases, amendments, parties, and governed property identifiers.

systems.name: Facilities management platform
systems.role: Tracks assets, inspections, work orders, and approved contractor activity.

systems.name: Property finance and tenant portal
systems.role: Provide budgets, authorized contacts, and controlled communication records.

flow.title: Authenticate tenant request
flow.description: Verify the requester, property, suite, and permitted scope before retrieving lease or service information.

flow.title: Resolve governing documents
flow.description: Find executed lease documents and amendments relevant to the request date, preserving unresolved version conflicts.

flow.title: Gather asset evidence
flow.description: Read equipment records and prior work orders; separate tenant observations from verified maintenance findings.

flow.title: Prepare service options
flow.description: Check approved vendor availability, access rules, and budget authority without assuming disputed cost responsibility.

flow.title: Route accountable review
flow.description: Present factual options to the property manager and refer contract interpretation to the appropriate qualified reviewer.

flow.title: Record approved response
flow.description: Create the authorized work request or communication with explicit scope and track vendor acceptance and tenant follow-up separately.

    S-->>O: Amendment missing from search index

diagrams.caption: An amendment is missing from the indexed lease packet. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: An amendment is missing from the indexed lease packet.
failures.detection: Document registry lists an executed revision absent from retrieval results.
failures.recovery: Stop obligation summaries, fetch the controlled document, and refresh the packet before review.

failures.scenario: A vendor quote exceeds the property manager's authority.
failures.detection: Budget and approval policy checks reject the proposed commitment.
failures.recovery: Route the exact quote and scope to the required approver without splitting work to evade the limit.

controls: Filter lease retrieval by property, tenant relationship, and assigned management role.
Distinguish direct clause citations from unresolved legal interpretation.
Require approval for vendor commitments, access grants, and binding tenant notices.
Preserve executed-document status and amendment precedence metadata.
Avoid exposing tenant financial or contractual details in shared facilities queues.

metrics.name: Document completeness
metrics.definition: Reviewed cases with all relevant executed amendments available divided by cases requiring lease evidence.

metrics.name: Service preparation time
metrics.definition: Time from authenticated request to manager-reviewable service options.

metrics.name: Authority rejection rate
metrics.definition: Proposed commitments blocked by approval limits divided by proposed commitments.

metrics.name: Response correction burden
metrics.definition: Material factual or citation corrections per reviewed tenant response.

tradeoffs.cost: Ambiguous wording still requires professional interpretation.

tradeoffs.benefit: Connects tenant requests to actual asset history.
tradeoffs.cost: Property identifiers and ownership records need reconciliation.
Budget and access approvals remain separate dependencies.

rollout.acceptance: Managers and qualified reviewers verify amendments, property identity, and unsupported legal conclusions.
One portfolio reviews draft packets after tenant isolation and document-access tests pass.
Controlled work requests launch after budget-limit, vendor-acceptance, and stale-amendment exercises succeed.
